title.en: Tissues in plants and animals and the musculoskeletal system

text.en: A football team needs players with different jobs. In a body, cells with the same job form a tissue. Plants and animals use different tissues because plants stay fixed while animals move.

A tissue is a group of similar cells that together perform a specific function.
Plants are fixed and need support, so their cells have walls and many tissues give strength. Animals move, so they need muscles and bones.
Plants grow at the tips of roots and shoots by apical meristem, which makes them longer.
Lateral meristem makes plants grow in girth, becoming thicker, and intercalary meristem helps grass grow again after grazing.
Permanent tissues include parenchyma (thin walls), collenchyma (unevenly thickened corners) and sclerenchyma, and the conducting tissues xylem and phloem.
In animals the main tissues are epithelial, connective, muscular and nervous. The cells of nervous tissue are called neurons.
The musculoskeletal system is made of bones, muscles, joints, cartilage, tendons and ligaments. Muscles pull on bones, attached by tendons, to produce movement.
Joints let bones move: ball and socket at the shoulder, pivot, hinge and fixed joints. The skeleton, with skull, backbone and rib cage, protects organs.

problem.en: Which tissue makes a root grow longer and which makes a stem thicker?

text.en: Growth in length takes place at the tips: apical meristem.
Growth in girth happens by lateral meristem.
So apical for length and lateral for thickness.

prompt.en: Name three plant tissues and two animal tissues with one function each.

requiredIdeas.en: Muscle moves bones; nerve carries signals

points.en: Tissues are groups of cells with a common function.
Animals have epithelial, connective, muscular and nervous tissues.
Bones, muscles and joints work together for movement.
